AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Plumbagin (5-hydroxy-2-methyl-1,4-napthoquinone) derived from Plumbago species is a potential anti-tumour agent. Plumbagin has been tested for anti-cancer activity in vitro and in vivo using mice model.

AbstractText.Label: AIM
AbstractText.content: To study the tumour suppressing efficacy of plumbagin using zebrafish model.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: Human Non-small lung cancer cell line were cultured in vitro and transplanted in to zebrafish. The development of tumour was confirmed by performing histology. The tumour was then allowed to progress in vivo and the fishes were administered with plumbagin orally for three continuous days. The tumour suppression capacity was monitored subsequently using transcriptosome analysis.

AbstractText.Label: STATISTICAL METHODS
AbstractText.content: The pixel integrated density obtained was converted into relative gene expression using IBM SPSS.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The administration of plumbagin had an ability to suppress tumour and the size of the tumour were relatively lesser when compared with the control sample; it has also increased p53 gene expression.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: The study helps to conclude that plumbagin is an effective anti-tumour agent against human cancer cells based on the study in vivo in zebrafish.
